title: Understanding Pilot Salary Australia: Hourly to Annual Pay Under the Air Pilots Award
description: Learn how to convert pilot salary Australia from hourly to annual using Fair Work Ombudsman rates. Includes award rates, casual loading, super, and tax estimates.
salarySummary: For a full-time pilot under the Air Pilots Award, annual salary is calculated as hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How do I convert an annual pilot salary to an hourly rate?
faqs.a: For full-time or part-time pilots, divide the annual salary by 52 to get the weekly rate, then divide by 38 to get the hourly rate. For casual pilots, divide the annual salary (including additions) by 800, then add 25% casual loading. This is specified in the Air Pilots Award and explained by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for pilots and how is it applied?
faqs.a: Casual pilots receive a 25% loading on top of the hourly rate calculated from the annual salary (1/800th of annual salary per flying hour). This loading compensates for entitlements like leave and is paid instead of those benefits. The loading is applied after calculating the base hourly rate.

faqs.q: How does superannuation work for pilots under the award?
faqs.a: Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of ordinary earnings on top of the base pay, up to the maximum contribution base ($270,830 for 2026–27). The award specifies that contributions go to a fund like AustralianSuper unless the employee chooses another eligible fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting hourly to annual pay

When you have an hourly rate, the simplest way to estimate your annual gross pay is to multiply that rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For full-time employees under most awards, including the Air Pilots Award, the standard ordinary hours are 38 per week. So the formula becomes:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $30, your annual pay would be about $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for comparing offers or understanding your pay.

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For a 38‑hour week, weekly pay = hourly rate × 38, so fortnightly pay = hourly rate × 76.

## Pilot salary australia under the Air Pilots Award

When researching **pilot salary australia**, the most authoritative source is the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Air Pilots Award 2020 (MA000046). Unlike many awards that list hourly rates, the Pilots Award only contains annual salaries. To convert those annual figures to an hourly rate, the Fair Work Ombudsman provides clear guidance:

- **Full‑time and part‑time pilots**: Divide the annual salary by 52 to get the weekly rate, then divide by 38 to get the hourly rate.
- **Casual pilots**: Divide the annual salary (including any applicable additions) by 800 to get the hourly rate per flying hour. Then add a 25% casual loading.

For example, the Pay Guide published 10 July 2026 shows rates for aerial application operations. A pilot with 0 to 1000 flying hours and less than 6 months experience has a weekly rate of $978.10, which equates to an hourly rate of $25.74. A pilot with more than 6 months experience or 1001–2000 hours earns $1,004.90 per week, or $26.44 per hour. These rates are for full‑time or part‑time employees. Casual aerial application pilots have a set daily rate instead of an hourly rate, as noted in the award.

It is important to compare these award rates with the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. The experienced aerial application rate matches the minimum wage, while the entry‑level rate is slightly below. However, award rates can be higher for other classifications, such as airline captains. For instance, the award lists hourly rates for Airbus A320 and Boeing 737 captains at $65.65 per hour plus a daily allowance of $138.85.

## Casual loading and superannuation

If you are a casual pilot, your hourly rate is calculated differently. Under clause 10 of the Air Pilots Award, the formula is:

**(Annual salary + annual applicable additions) ÷ 800 = hourly rate**

Then multiply by 1.25 to include the 25% casual loading. This loading is paid instead of entitlements like annual leave, personal leave, and public holidays. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides an example: a casual pilot flying a piston engine aircraft with a total annual salary and additions of $80,741.53 would have a casual hourly rate of $126.16 per flying hour.

Superannuation is paid on top of your base pay. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund. The award specifies that contributions must go to a fund such as AustralianSuper unless you choose another eligible fund.

## Tax and take‑home pay

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of generally 2% of taxable income. The tax‑free threshold is included. Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted in this estimate.

For a quick estimate, you can use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool or check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for current rates. If you are comparing a salary offer, remember that super is paid on top of the advertised salary, so your total remuneration package is higher.

## Putting it all together

When you see a **pilot salary australia** figure, whether it is an hourly rate or an annual salary, you now have the tools to convert between them. Always check the specific classification in the Air Pilots Award, as rates vary by aircraft type, experience, and employment type. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool can help you calculate exact pay including allowances and penalties.

Remember that the annual estimate from an hourly rate assumes 38 hours per week, 52 weeks per year. If you work fewer hours or have unpaid breaks, your actual annual pay will differ. For casuals, the 25% loading significantly increases the hourly rate, but you do not receive paid leave.

For more details on how super and packaging affect your total pay, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page. And if you need to calculate your take‑home pay after tax, visit [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home).
